note: Leaving a canvas with nothing new since its last sync asks Dropbox nothing: the ledger knows what Dropbox holds, and the saver's queue reads only canvas.json, two headers and the log's length.
A new canvas's first sync: canvas.json and the log (its header and records) as one part. No folder is made first; an upload makes its folders.
After 10 new strokes: one upload, the log's new whole records as one part (ink.log.parts/<generation>/<offset>.part). canvas.json and the snapshot are unchanged, so they don't go.

Bytes uploaded after 10 new strokes, minus the bytes those strokes appended to the log: the tail and nothing else. Uploading the whole log instead would send every stroke since the last compaction, up to 1 MB or the snapshot's size, every time.
The sync after a compaction: the new log's first part, the new snapshot (once; later syncs don't send it), and one delete of the replaced generation's parts.
Bytes uploaded after a compaction, minus the new snapshot and the new log: nothing else goes.
A sheet's PDF (sheets/<content hash>.pdf) uploads once, with the sync after it was placed.
Never again: the ledger remembers each PDF uploaded, by name.

The folder check, before the first upload after the engine starts, the app comes back to the foreground or the connection returns: one list_folder/continue of Vellum/ since the cursor kept in the ledger (the first ever, or after a reset, is one recursive list_folder). None at all when nothing is waiting to upload, and none on the syncs between.

The sync after a canvas's folder was deleted on the laptop, for a canvas with one sheet and no snapshot: the folder check, then the whole canvas once (the sheet's PDF, canvas.json, the log as one part). A canvas with a snapshot adds one upload, each further sheet one.
Bytes uploaded rebuilding a deleted folder, minus the canvas's files on the Duo (canvas.json, the log, the snapshot, the sheets' PDFs): each goes once, nothing else.
The sync after the re-upload, with new strokes: back to the log's tail alone, with no folder check.

Leaving a canvas with sync on does no storage file work on the main thread: closing hands the flush to the saver's queue, and queueing the sync is a hop to the sync actor, which writes its ledger and reads the canvas off the main thread.
